nodes.label: minimaCore Desktop App
nodes.rationale: A native desktop app that runs the minimaCore node locally and wears the same UI as the Minima native Android apps, starting with a self-custody wallet. Development software, not affiliated with Minima Global.

nodes.label: Thin Wrapper Around minima.jar
nodes.rationale: Design intent: rather than reimplementing a node, the app is a thin wrapper around an ever-updating minima.jar — it bundles a known-good jar + a JRE, launches the node headless with RPC, and can pull newer jars from GitHub releases as the upstream project develops.

nodes.label: Bundled JRE (no system Java needed)
nodes.rationale: The app ships a jlink-minimized JRE (java.se + jdk.unsupported) at resources/jre so no system Java is required to run the node.

nodes.label: First-run Node Wizard
nodes.rationale: First run lets the user pick network (Mainnet / Solo-test / Custom peer) plus advanced options (data folder, port, full-history).

nodes.label: Wallet Seed Onboarding (megammrsync restore + key-uses attestation)
nodes.rationale: New (fresh seed, backed up) or Restore from seed — restore fast-syncs via megammrsync in seconds. The WOTS key-uses attestation (0 for new, prior count for a restore) exists because WOTS one-time signatures are unsafe if a key-use counter is understated.

nodes.label: Node Updater (sha256-verified jar swap)
nodes.rationale: Checks a GitHub releases feed for a newer minima.jar, verifies sha256 before swapping, then restarts the node. TODO notes the updater repo still needs pinning.

nodes.label: Localhost-only RPC with Keychain-held Password
nodes.rationale: The node is launched with -rpcenable true -rpcpassword <secret> -daemon; RPC is localhost-only and the password is kept in the macOS Keychain to keep the local node off the network attack surface.

nodes.label: Design.java CSS Port (native look)
nodes.rationale: Reuses the native Design.java look via renderer/style.css — a 1:1 CSS port shared with the PandaPools MiniDapp (dark #0A0A0F, Minima-orange #F7931A, light/dark/original themes) — so the desktop matches the native Android apps instead of inventing a new design.
